headline: Singapore's Grab lifts annual forecasts as AI, incentives drive growth
body_text: Singapore's Grab raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on Tuesday, encouraged by strong demand for its ride-hailing and delivery services driven by promotional offers, driver incentives and its AI initiatives. Grab now expects revenue between $4.10 billion and $4.15 billion for 2026, compared with its prior projection of $4.04 billion to $4.10 billion, and marginally above market estimates. The company also raised its forecast for annual adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) to between $720 million and $740 million, from $700 million to $720 million earlier. Second-quarter revenue rose 22% to $997 million, beating analysts' estimate of $990.8 million. Gross merchandise value (GMV) across mobility and delivery services climbed 21% to $6.5 billion. Grab, the biggest ride-hailing and delivery firm in Southeast Asia, has banked on features including order bundling and a budget-friendly tier called 'Saver' to target cost-conscious customers grappling with higher fuel prices following the Iran war. The company invested $706 million in customer and partner incentives in the second quarter, including more than $7 million to support driver earnings during the fuel crisis. The company also announced a new $750 million share buyback program. The upbeat projections and the new buyback pushed shares of the Nasdaq-listed company up 4% in extended trading. CFO Peter Oey said the strategy was 'intentionally designed so prices would continue to be very, very low for customers, and drivers would be on the road despite high fuel prices.' He said AI investments meant 'the cost structure is getting better and better', enabling product delivery three times faster than previously while eliminating nearly 40,000 sales inefficiency hours.
